answer: DriveTexas is not runtime-registered by county or community. The live connector is a statewide shared in-memory feed, spatially projected after fetch. A browser can show records only when the shared key was supplied to that page and a fetch succeeded (including records retained in memory after a later failure), or through the separate legacy TxDOT runtime store; repository snapshots and fixtures are audit-only and cannot render. A fresh Dallas page with configurationSource none had none of the three accepted script-global sources, so it could not fetch.

endpointTemplatePrecedence: built-in DriveTexas conditions GeoJSON endpoint template
configuration.substitution: The selected key is URL-encoded into the {api_key} placeholder.
configuration.noneMeaning: All three accepted key values were absent, non-string, empty, or whitespace when runtime diagnostics were read.

browserPersistence.localStorage: No key or record persistence. localStorage may only opt in loading js/gridly.local.js through gridlyLocal=true.
browserPersistence.cacheStorage: Not used; connector requests use cache no-store.
browserPersistence.inPrivateConclusion: Private browsing does not erase a DriveTexas key because Gridly never stores it in browser storage. It can remove the optional gridlyLocal loader opt-in flag, but the key must still come from the local script/global, not storage. InPrivate is therefore not the direct cause of configurationSource none.

configuration.localDevelopment: Unconfigured by default. An owner may create the gitignored js/gridly.local.js using the documented PowerShell setup and opt in to loading it with the gridlyLocal URL/localStorage flag or GRIDLY_ENABLE_LOCAL_OVERRIDES global.
configuration.deployment: No tracked build, GitHub workflow, GitHub Pages, preview, production, Supabase, or hosting configuration injects a DriveTexas key. Repository evidence does not support claiming deployed Gridly is configured differently. A deployment may serve an untracked/generated local override only through an external process not evidenced here.

activation.path: gridlyOfficialProviderActivation schedules activate, which calls the same gridlyDriveTexasConnector.startPolling for every selected area
activation.dallasExplanation: activated and driveTexasActivated only prove startPolling existed and was invoked. startPolling schedules fetchNow; buildEndpoint then fails because no accepted key source exists.

geographicApplicability.selectionBehavior: One complete statewide normalized array is filtered/proven against the selected awareness area by coordinates, geometry, radius, and limited text fallback.
geographicApplicability.legacyMetadata: The intelligence.drivetexas package lists eleven Southeast Texas supportedCommunities, but explicitly marks runtimeActivationPerformed and transportationIntelligenceActivated false and behavior/read-path changes false. It is controlled-migration metadata, not a live connector gate.

visibleDataPaths.path: live DriveTexas connector -> complete in-memory records -> LP039 authority -> consumer projection
visibleDataPaths.qualification: A new fetch cannot start without a key.

visibleDataPaths.path: connector retained last-successful records after a later fetch/configuration failure
visibleDataPaths.qualification: Only within the same loaded page because the complete and awareness arrays are module memory; no reload/browser persistence.
The authority resolver prefers connector records; provider storage is also page memory and has no static or persistent seed.

visibleDataPaths.path: legacy gridlyTxdot service -> gridlyExternalRoadConditions -> futureTxdotIncidents/futureTxdotConstruction/map and unified incident consumers
visibleDataPaths.qualification: This is a separate official-roadway runtime path sharing GRIDLY_CONFIG.txdot.apiKey/GRIDLY_TXDOT_API_KEY. If its page-memory store was prepopulated or its configuration timing differed, TxDOT-labelled records can render even when the newer connector audit is unconfigured; it has no browser persistence and clears its arrays on its own missing-key/fetch failure.
It derives from loaded connector/provider records; injected records exist for audit/test calls, not normal production loading.

visibleDataPaths.path: static exports, replay fixtures, LP044 inventory, county evidence, or package evidence
visibleDataPaths.qualification: All discovered material is audit-only/non-production or passive generated evidence and is not loaded into consumer stores.

visibleDataPaths.path: Supabase, community reports, weather, crossings, county packages, or another official-source layer
visibleDataPaths.qualification: These can independently show their own information but do not manufacture DriveTexas connector records.

representativeCounties.staticOrRetainedExplanation: No renderable static fallback; only same-page retained memory after an earlier success. Owner evidence instead proves no key and no retained data.

Numerous Liberty DriveTexas fixtures/exports and historical evidence exist, but are audit-only and cannot render. Same-page live retained memory or the separate TxDOT runtime store can explain an observation.
Legacy package metadata names harris-tx but is not a runtime gate or fallback. Only live/page-memory paths can render.

representativeCounties.community: representative additional county appearing in repository DriveTexas fixtures/metadata
representativeCounties.staticOrRetainedExplanation: Repository export samples mention Montgomery but are explicitly audit-only/non-production; county evidence also says DriveTexas paused. They do not prove consumer-visible production records.

defectsAndRisks: No tracked deployment-time key injection exists, so an ordinary fresh checkout/deployment is unconfigured unless an external owner process supplies a script global.
The optional local override loader is opt-in and its dynamic script is not a documented deployment injection mechanism.

Two shared live paths (the newer DriveTexas connector and legacy TxDOT service) consume overlapping globals but maintain separate in-memory stores and diagnostics, which can make owner observations appear inconsistent.
Legacy Southeast Texas supportedCommunities metadata resembles an allowlist despite being explicitly non-activating; it can mislead audits but does not restrict runtime.
Retained records survive connector failure in page memory, so visible data does not prove the current fetch or current configuration succeeded.
recommendation: Treat Dallas as a shared configuration/deployment failure, not a county-registration defect. First identify the exact deployed script/global injection process and capture both the DriveTexas connector audit and legacy gridlyTxdot diagnostics in the same page. Do not add county registrations or patch runtime in LP214 Phase 2.3.
